headline: SilverEdge deal and margin gains drive a strong quarter
summary_short: Revenue rose to $1,906M (+1.5% y/y) as the SilverEdge acquisition and contract ramp-up offset completions; net income jumped to $115M (+69.1% y/y, diluted EPS $2.61) on improved contract profitability, a $12M investment-sale gain, and lower SG&A.
summary_long: Revenue grew $29M y/y to $1,906M: Defense & Intelligence +$33M (SilverEdge contributed $19M, plus contract ramp-up), partly offset by Civilian's -$4M (contract completions). Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 11.6% (from 8.4%) on improved contract profitability, a $12M gain on sale of an investment, and lower SG&A. Effective tax rate held near flat at 20.9% (20.6% prior year) on R&D credits and the FDII deduction. Operating cash flow rose $27M y/y to $127M on payment timing. SAIC repurchased $175M of stock (1.9M shares) and paid a $0.37/share dividend; total backlog was $22,860M with $2.1B of net bookings this quarter. No forward revenue/EPS guidance appears in the 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Revenue grew on the SilverEdge acquisition and contract ramp-up; margins and net income rose further on improved contract profitability, a one-time $12M investment-sale gain, and lower SG&A.

Revenues rose $29M y/y primarily from the SilverEdge acquisition ($19M) and ramp-up on existing/new contracts, partly offset by contract completions; ex-SilverEdge organic growth was approximately 0.5%.
Cost of revenues fell to 86.9% of revenue from 88.9% the prior year; gross profit is the arithmetic difference between reported Revenues and Cost of revenues.
Operating income as a percentage of revenue rose y/y on improved profitability across the contract portfolio and a $12M gain from the sale of an investment.
Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 11.6% from 8.4%, driven by improved contract profitability, the $12M investment-sale gain, and lower SG&A expense.
Net income rose on higher operating income plus the investment-sale gain; effective tax rate was roughly flat at 20.9% vs 20.6%, aided by R&D tax credits and the FDII deduction.
Diluted EPS rose in line with net income growth, aided by a lower share count from ongoing buybacks (1.9 million shares repurchased this quarter).
